title: American Chestnut: Ancient American Chestnuts You Can Visit
meta_description: A tree the blight all but erased. Two flank the O. O. Howard House in Vancouver, Washington, and Tacoma's has a trunk about 4.2 metres round.
intro: American chestnut was once among the commonest trees of the eastern forests, until a fungus arrived in the early twentieth century and killed almost all of them. The survivors we map grew far from those forests. In Vancouver, Washington, two stand at either end of the 1878 O. O. Howard House on Officers Row, the larger about 4.2 metres round and 27 metres tall; the city estimates that only 300 to 500 mature American chestnuts remain. In Tacoma, the Heritage Tree register lists one in Wright Park with a trunk 53 inches across, about 4.2 metres round, standing near a European sweet chestnut so that the two can be compared. And a reader sent us one from City Park in Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, with two grey trunks rising from a single base.
